Elementκ-carbide behaviorEffect on microstructureMechanical properties>
SiPromotes intragranular κ-carbide formation, accelerates nucleation, increases carbon partitioning; excessive Si may promote intergranular κ-carbidesRefines grain structure, enhances Al and C activity, risk of red scale defect with excess SiIncreases yield strength (up to 950 MPa), reduces elongation slightly
CrSuppresses intergranular κ-carbides, promotes fine intragranular κ-carbides, delays precipitation at low contentRefines grains, stabilizes austenite, suppresses DO3 at moderate content, enhances oxidation resistanceIncreases yield strength, improves corrosion resistance, maintains ductility
CuEnhances κ-carbide precipitation when co-precipitated with Cu-rich clusters; refines particlesRefines grains, stabilizes austenite, suppresses recrystallization, promotes Cu-B2 phaseImproves strength (808 MPa) and ductility (20%-40%) via dual strengthening
VCan hinder κ-carbide formation by binding carbon; dual precipitation of VC and κ-carbidesRefines grains, precipitates VC in γ and α phases, impedes recrystallizationIncreases strength (to >1300 MPa), enhances ductility (~41%)
NbNbC precipitates compete with κ-carbides; delays their precipitation and promotes finer carbidesRefines austenite grains, precipitates fine NbC particlesEnhances strength (UTS >900 MPa), improves elongation by ≈6%
MoPartially substitutes κ-carbides with Mo2C; delays recrystallization and modifies precipitation behaviorRefines structure, increases recrystallization temp, stabilizes grain boundariesIncreases strength (680 MPa), hardness; slight ductility loss at high content
NiReduces size of κ-carbides and modifies composition; co-precipitates NiAl (B2) and κ-carbidesPromotes δ-ferrite formation, stabilizes NiAl phase, reduces κ-carbide sizeStrength >1300 MPa, elongation 22%-27%; enhances creep resistance
